title: Conservativity of geometric stalks on the derived category
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme and let $K\to L$ be a morphism of complexes in
$\Dplus(T_{\Et})$ of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Then $K\to L$ is an
isomorphism of $\Dplus(T_{\Et})$ if and only if for every geometric point
[def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] $\bar t$ of $T$ and every integer $i$ the
induced map

$$
 \mathcal H^i(K)_{\bar t}\longrightarrow\mathcal H^i(L)_{\bar t}
$$

of geometric stalks is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Apply Mathlib DerivedCategory.Plus.isIso_iff, the exact cohomology criterion of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-plus-iso-on-cohomology], to reduce invertibility of f to invertibility of every cohomology-sheaf map. No separate roof construction or calculus-of-fractions import is needed.

For each cohomological degree i, apply Scheme.isIso_of_isIso_sheafFiber_map from [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. Its family uses the universe-lifted point at the algebraic closure of each residue field. Specialize the hypothesis to that algebraically closed field and Scheme.algClosurePoint. Transport invertibility from the ordinary stalk to the universe-lifted stalk by NatIso.isIso_map_iff applied to the proved GrothendieckTopology.Point.uliftSheafFiberIso. This gives all the stalk hypotheses of the conservative-family theorem and hence invertibility of H^i(f).

Conversely, if f is invertible, both the cohomology functor and the geometric-stalk functor of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] preserve its inverse. The two functor-map IsIso instances prove every displayed stalk map invertible.
